newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan ends up against US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan ends up against US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed up at 8.2920 on Monday from last Friday's 8.2928 against the U.S. dollar in Shanghai on market expectations that China would post a solid foreign trade surplus for May, traders said.
The weighted average price on Friday was 8.2932.
Beijing is due to announce foreign trade statistics for May in the next week.
"Pro-yuan sentiment has grown again with the approach of the date for announcing the May foreign trade statistics," one trader said. "This supported the yuan's upward trend today."

The yuan opened higher at 8.2924 and consolidated in a narrow range of 8.2920 and an intraday low of 8.2925 for most of the session, hitting a high of 8.2916. Trading was dull with most business done at 8.2922, traders said.
Despite Monday's rise, traders said a wait-and-see attitude was strong on the market because of the central bank's intervention to depress the local currency last Thursday.
"This attitude limited the yuan's rising momentum, making it stick to a narrow range today," a second trader said.
Traders said they expected the yuan to move around the 8.2920 level on Tuesday.
The yuan closed down at 7.3502 from 7.1465 against 100 Japanese yen and slightly down at an intraday low of 1.0703 from 1.0700 against the Hong Kong dollar.
